summary: More data helped, but cross-site prediction remains weak. A useful PhD should target one clinical decision and measure when a model must abstain.
problem:
EEG: scalp electrical activity.
BOLD: blood oxygenation in fMRI.
One useful clinical decision?
takeaway: The small MLP and sparse ECG pipeline did not improve the EEG baseline. Regional gain beyond a predicted-global template remains uncertain: paired delta-r .004 (95% CI -.008 to .017). These tests do not establish a biological ceiling.
methods: ds006040: 27 people/54 runs; three subject-grouped outer folds, separate inner tuning. Ridge/small MLP; EEG, sparse ECG timing/availability, or both. Cross 4/12 training people and 120/240 retained target-seconds/person. Fixed subsets; one neural seed; four equal-weight MLP target groups. Published models were not reproduced.
work_packages: Which montage, EEG history and sensors add held-out value for their acquisition cost?
Can shared dynamics and counted calibration improve regional signal beyond ridge and state controls?
What error is achievable at useful coverage under specified shift? Compare abstention with quality rejection.
clinical_gate:
First route: wakefulness advisory; compare direct EEG arousal prediction.
Second route: one regional feedback target; require paired patient validation and controlled benefit.
Precedent: Prism is cleared for adjunctive PTSD biofeedback; diagnostic interpretation excluded [4].
Limits: retrospective preprocessing; normalized targets, no absolute %BOLD calibration; sparse ECG, one development site/seed. Live use and clinical benefit untested [5].
references:
